visual_logic: Isolates a single leaf-shaped tooth to showcase the highly unique herbivorous adaptation of this specialized coelurosaurian theropod, contrasting with predatory theropod teeth.
prompt: High-fidelity 3D asset render of a single fossilized leaf slicer tooth from a Therizinosaurus, executed in a 3D animated feature film aesthetic with soft, stylized contours. The specimen exhibits a prominent lanceolate or 'leaf-shaped' crown morphology: it is broad, somewhat flattened, and possesses large, coarse, distinct serrations along the cutting margins designed for shearing plant material. The fossil coloration features a dark, mineralized charcoal and dark brown enamel patina with a subtle matte sheen. The single tooth is isolated and oriented vertically, centered precisely on a 1:1 square canvas. The background is a seamless, solid light-grey studio plane that fills the entire canvas without any internal decorative lines, borders, or boxes. The asset is scaled down to maintain a strict 25% empty background margin on all four sides to completely protect against UI clipping. Grounded flat on the floor plane with realistic, soft contact shadows. A clean checkered black-and-white scientific scale bar sits centered at the bottom.
